page: The UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL4 is an x86_64 architecture cloud server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 20 shared vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.8 GB per vCPU. The server is equipped with two NVIDIA L4 graphics processing units based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM.

This configuration does not include local storage, meaning external block storage must be attached for persistent data. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated CPU instances, though the substantial memory capacity and dual GPU accelerators offset this for specific workloads.

Given the dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs and 256 GB of RAM, this server is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and video transcoding. The high memory density relative to the shared CPU count offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-heavy and GPU-bound tasks that do not require continuous, dedicated single-core CPU performance.
